name: Desphi Satria Nurjaya

portfolio.title: Ceria Belajar · Test Automation
portfolio.intro: An end-to-end test suite for my own app, Ceria Belajar. Because the app is mine, everything is public: the code, the CI pipeline, and the live test report.
points: 72 automated test runs covering child profiles, medals, and stars, on desktop and a mobile viewport.

Found 3 bugs in the app’s reward system: 19 of 32 medals unlocked the wrong reward, the medal counter skipped one medal, and two screens showed different star counts for the same child. All three are fixed and now guarded by regression tests.
Surfaced accessibility gaps (controls that could not be used with a keyboard or screen reader, and an animation that ignored the reduce-motion setting) and fixed them in the app.
Readable reporting: every test states what it verifies and reads as Given / When / Then steps in the Allure report.
notes: **Approach:** Page Object Model, test data seeded through localStorage instead of slow UI setup, accessibility-first locators, and known bugs tracked as expected-failure tests that flag themselves once the fix ships.
**Tools:** Playwright, TypeScript, GitHub Actions, Allure, GitHub Pages.

portfolio.title: Test Automation Suites
portfolio.intro: 550+ automated test cases across four suites that I lead and contribute to, all following one consistent structure. The code is proprietary, so this is a high-level overview.
points: **Public API** (Playwright): 200+ test cases
**Formulir Web checkout** (Playwright): 200+ test cases
**Mengantar Web App** (Playwright): 100+ test cases
**Formulir Mobile** (Maestro Studio): 50+ test cases
notes: **Approach:** Page Object Model, reusable fixtures, per-environment configuration, test data generated per run, and tests tagged by type (smoke, regression) and feature.
**Delivery:** run on GitHub Actions, with Allure reports for the team to review.
**Tools:** Playwright, Maestro Studio, TypeScript, GitHub Actions, Allure.

caseStudy.title: Standardizing QA Across 6 Squads
caseStudy.problem: Our QA team (about 14 engineers across 6 squads) had no shared standard. Each QA used their own tools, test case format, and workflow. QA’s role inside each squad was barely visible: our work was seen as “just testing,” even though QA contributed from requirements all the way to release.
caseStudy.goal: Give every squad one way of working, and make QA’s contribution visible and measurable beyond test execution.
actions: Wrote the QA Guide Book: QA principles and mindset, QA’s role in every SDLC phase, and shared standards for task creation, test cases, bug reports, hotfix handling, and release preparation.

Designed a metrics framework: Feedback Adoption Rate, Early Feedback Ratio, Test Execution and Pass Rate, Feedback Fix Rate, and Defect Detection/Escape Percentage, each with a formula and clear thresholds.
Reviewed every standard and metric with the QA team before rollout, so each squad agreed on the approach before adopting it.
Introduced a quarterly QA audit that reports these metrics per squad.
results: **Shift-left in practice:** QA is now involved from pre-grooming and design review, not only after development.
**Useful beyond QA:** engineers use the per-sprint Fix Rate recap to complete their own sprint reports.
**Trusted by management:** the quarterly QA report is used to assess QA KPIs and serves as the evidence for quarterly performance bonuses.
caseStudy.next: Back every explanation of a metric drop with data, add owners and targets to each action item, define explicit release go/no-go criteria and hotfix severity levels, and keep refining metric thresholds based on real usage.
